Subject: Re: Redwood Private/VPC pricing — next steps & budget

Hi Alex — great speaking earlier. Quick recap and next steps:

- Scope: Private VPC deployment for EnterpriseNet, initial pilot for payments-review workflows.
- Environments: you mentioned dev + staging + prod (3 total) — confirm?
- Volume: you said "small pilot then scale" — need concrete starting avg/month and 12-month target (tokens/month).
- Licensing preference: did you lean toward subscription (per-environment) or enterprise license (flat + overages)?
- Support: confirm desired tier (Standard / Premium / Enterprise SLA).

Attached: MAP (mutual_action_plan.xlsx), pricing_estimate_v1.pdf

Can you confirm the bullets above and share:
1) current expected tokens/month for pilot and 12-mo target
2) target $/1M tokens or budget range for inference (ballpark)
3) any compliance/KMS/throughput constraints

Thanks — I'll follow up with ballpark scenarios after you confirm.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Redwood Private/VPC pricing — next steps & budget

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the call. Confirming the items you asked for: 

- Environments: yes, dev + staging + prod (3).
- Pilot volumes: roughly 10M tokens/month for the pilot (first 2 months).
- 12-month target: we expect to grow to ~45M tokens/month if the pilot goes well.
- Budget: ballpark range we're thinking about is $40k–$70k/month for the solution (covers infra + license/support).
- Target unit economics: we're aiming for somewhere around $1,000–$1,500 per 1M tokens depending on SLA and support — lower is better, but open to structure (flat license vs per-token).

Compliance: we need KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and SOC2 attestation. Throughput: peak throughput during batch runs ~1200 tokens/sec sustained for short windows.

Can you sketch two or three pricing options (subscription per env vs enterprise license vs reserved capacity) and how they map to $/1M tokens? Also include support tier definitions. Procurement will want ranges so we can discuss internally this afternoon.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Platforms, EnterpriseNet
alex.j@enterprisenet.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@enterprisenet.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Private/VPC pricing — next steps & budget

Thanks Alex — really helpful. Below are three ballpark scenarios based on the volumes you gave (pilot 10M/mo -> scale 45M/mo). These are high-level — we can firm up numbers once you confirm env count, KMS, and term.

Option A — Subscription (per-environment)
- Model: $8,000 per environment / month (includes infra orchestration, runtime, updates).
- Inclusions: per-env includes up to 10M tokens/month of inference capacity; overage = $900 / 1M tokens.
- Example math for 45M tokens, 3 envs: base = $8k * 3 = $24k/mo + overage on 35M = 35 * $900 = $31.5k => total ~$55.5k/mo (~$1,233 / 1M tokens effective).

Option B — Enterprise license (12-mo term)
- Model: annual license $400,000 / year (~$33.3k/mo) for up to 50M tokens/month included; overage = $700 / 1M tokens.
- Example: for 45M tokens, cost ~ $33.3k/mo effective (~$740 / 1M tokens if you amortize included capacity).

Option C — Dedicated reserved capacity (Private Dedicated)
- Model: fixed monthly reserved capacity (custom), recommended for sustained high throughput. Typical starting point: $60k–$80k/mo with capacity guarantees and lower per-token marginals.

Support tiers (adds to base price):
- Standard (included): business-hours email support, 1 business-day response for P1.
- Premium (+20%): 24/7 on-call, 4-hour P1 response, phone escalation, named CSM.
- Enterprise (+40%): 24/7 follow-the-sun, 1-hour P1, assigned technical account team, quarterly on-site reviews / runbooks.

KMS & compliance: customer-managed KMS + SOC2 is supported in Private/VPC. We'll include required attestation artifacts and network diagrams in the SOW.

Next steps: I attached pricing_estimate_v2.pdf with the scenario math and a short MAP. If you like Option B (enterprise license) I can put together a formal quote and draft SOW for procurement.

—Marissa
P.S. for procurement: what's your PO process and typical approval lead time?
From: Procurement <procurement@enterprisenet.com>

Subject: Internal: Recommended offer for EnterpriseNet (DEAL-4857)

Internal only — quick alignment before I send formal quote: 
- Recommended commercial: Option B (Enterprise license)
  - 12-mo term, $400k/year (includes up to 50M tokens/month).
  - Support: Enterprise tier (+40%).
  - Environments: 3 (dev/staging/prod).
  - Onboarding: include first-month credits for the pilot (first 10M tokens free) and 2 dedicated onboarding calls.
- Why: hits their target $/1M (amortized), simpler procurement path, protects unit economics as they scale to 45M+/mo.

Action items:
- Ben: please prep a redline-friendly quote + SOW and include required compliance artifacts (SOC2 report, KMS integration notes).
- Rishi: please confirm approval for the 12-mo list price and Enterprise support uplift; also confirm whether we can include the onboarding credit.

I will follow up to procurement with DocuSign envelope once you both confirm.

—Marissa
